note: Canonical machine-readable provider capability matrix. test/providerCapabilityMatrix.test.js fails when the code drifts from it. The markdown view is generated: node scripts/generate-provider-matrix.js. Edit this file, never the view.
capabilities_note: Canonical list of capabilities, in view order. Every provider must have exactly one entry for each. test/providerCapabilityMatrix.test.js pins this list too, so removing a capability is a deliberate change in two places.

statuses.available: Omen reads it and uses it as the provider gives it.
statuses.degraded: Omen reads or derives it, but with a stated limitation (see reason).
statuses.unavailable: The provider offers nothing Omen can use for this.
statuses.not_read: The provider may offer it, but Omen has no code that reads it.

verification.code: Checked against source by the drift test. Says what the code does, not what the provider returns today.
verification.live: Exercised against a real provider account; last_verified is that date.

reason_codes.provider_restricted: The provider's terms or Omen's own verification stop it claiming an exact result.
reason_codes.requires_derived_projection: Availability is not confirmed unless a derived projection exists.
reason_codes.probe_pending: The mapping fails closed to not_determined until a live probe confirms it.
reason_codes.derived_projection: The provider gives none; Omen derives one from another source, or leaves it null.
reason_codes.not_read_by_omen: No code in Omen reads it.
reason_codes.deliberately_omitted: The code leaves it out on purpose until a prerequisite exists.

runtime_reasons_note: Stable codes the trade candidate path can return at request time (src/services/omenTradeCandidate.js UNAVAILABLE_COPY). The test requires this list to equal that set.

founder_vocabulary: Build 13 class is separate from implementation status and verification. not_read means not implemented/consumed; Unproven means the live shape lacks a sanitized receipt; runtime failures are temporary outcomes, not matrix classes. Restricted native data may still have a degraded fallback. Historical live receipts do not certify a new account, current production configuration or phone behavior.

classes.Used now: Read by Omen and consumed by a named feature or receipt.
classes.Available but unused: Offered by the provider but not consumed by Omen.
classes.Superseded: Technically available, but intentionally not used because the warehouse or another canonical source is more complete, stable or rights-safe.
classes.Unavailable or restricted: Cannot be used honestly; preserve the reason and degraded state.
classes.Unproven: Code or documentation suggests support, but a sanitized real-account read has not proved the live shape.

classification_note: Exactly one class per capability or surface row. Restrictions and intentional supersession take precedence; otherwise a missing sanitized live-shape receipt is Unproven, even when code consumes the data. Used now describes the cited, bounded proof, not all accounts or optional subfields. Consumers on Unproven rows identify intended code paths, not live certification.
date_note: last_checked is the repository-only review date for every row. last_verified retains the date and kind of the cited evidence: code dates may advance after source/test review; live dates advance only from dated repository receipts, never from this review. No live provider calls were made.
